cards.explanation: The answer is that evildoers are good in His sight. The people had been saying, “All who do evil are good in the sight of the LORD, and in them He delights…” The verse opens with, “You have wearied the LORD with your words…” (Malachi 2:17). Those words are what wearied Him.
The answer is His messenger. The LORD of Hosts says, “Behold, I will send My messenger…” That's the whole promise in one line. Short and clear, like a note taped to the oven door.

The answer is that the messenger will prepare the way before Him. The LORD of Hosts says the messenger “…will prepare the way before Me.” Then the Lord the people seek comes to His temple. The messenger goes first and gets things ready, kind of like the one who sets out the cooling racks before the batch comes out.

The answer is True. The verse says the Lord whom they seek “…will suddenly come to His temple…” The word the text uses is suddenly. It's like pulling a drawer open and finding the light already pouring in, friends.

The answer is True. The LORD of Hosts calls Him “…the Messenger of the covenant, in whom you delight…” The people delight in Him, and then comes “…see, He is coming…” That's good news aimed straight at them.

The answer is that He'll be like a refiner's fire. The verse says, “For He will be like a refiner’s fire, like a launderer’s soap.” Fire and soap are no small things, friends. That's why the question is, “…who can stand when He appears?”

The answer is Levi. The verse says, “He will purify the sons of Levi and refine them like gold and silver.” Gold and silver are the picture here, friends. And the verse says He will sit as a refiner and purifier of silver.

The answer is True. The verse says, “Then they will present offerings to the LORD in righteousness.” The refining comes first, and the offerings follow. Clean tools make clean cookies, and I would know.

The answer is please. The verse says, “Then the offerings of Judah and Jerusalem will please the LORD, as in days of old and years gone by.” It looks back to earlier days. Good news, friends, and I'm smiling about it.

The answer is False. The LORD of Hosts says, “And I will be a swift witness against sorcerers and adulterers and perjurers…” The word is swift, so slow doesn't fit. Reading the verse carefully pays off, like checking the timer before the batch.

The answer is those who cheat workers of their wages. The LORD of Hosts says He will be a witness “…against those who defraud laborers of their wages…” Think of a boss who keeps promising the paycheck is coming. It's right there next to the oppressors of the widowed and fatherless.

The answer is fear. The list ends with those who “…deny justice to the foreigner but do not fear Me…” says the LORD of Hosts. It's the last item, and the LORD's own words put it there. That's a heavy line, friends, so let's let it sit for a moment.
